reasoning: Preserved all failure-driven edits because they address distinct answer-form, visual-evidence, and referent-resolution failures. Added the success-driven guidance on weighing apparently conflicting snippets and checking entity or timeframe distinctions, since that pattern is not covered by the failure edits. No edits target the protected section.

edits.target: For fragmentary quotes, titles, nicknames, or familiar sayings and proverbs, infer the omitted word or phrase that completes the clue rather than echoing the supplied text.
edits.content: For fragmentary quotes, titles, nicknames, or familiar sayings and proverbs, infer omitted wording when the clue explicitly asks for a completion. If the clue instead asks to identify a work or its title while giving only part of the title, return the full conventional title, not just the omitted word or supplied fragment.

edits.target: Use a name form that uniquely identifies the entity: give the complete identifying name when needed, but a surname or shorter form is appropriate when it is unambiguous. Do not add explanations or descriptive qualifiers unless requested.
edits.content: Use a name form that uniquely identifies the entity: give the complete identifying name when needed, but a surname or shorter form is appropriate when it is unambiguous. When a clue asks for one person, role, or term, return one answer rather than alternatives joined by “or”; choose the form most directly supported by clue-matching evidence. If a person appears under both a nickname and a full name, use the form explicitly used in the evidence that best matches the clue; prefer the full name when that evidence identifies them by it or when needed to disambiguate. Do not add explanations or descriptive qualifiers unless requested.

For clues referring to an item “seen here” or otherwise relying on a depiction, identify the depicted item from visual evidence when available; do not substitute a familiar product merely because it is salient in the surrounding text. If the depiction is unavailable and the text supports multiple candidates, do not treat one as established without distinguishing evidence.

When relevant snippets appear to conflict, assess which evidence best supports the full combination of clue details. Check whether apparent contradictions reflect different entities or timeframes before rejecting an otherwise well-supported candidate.

edits.target: Treat grammatical relations as target cues: wording such as “this state's X” asks for the state, not X's divisions, members, or examples. Use context to identify the entity filling the possessive or relational slot.
edits.content: Treat grammatical relations as target cues: wording such as “this state's X” asks for the state, not X's divisions, members, or examples. Resolve pronouns and demonstratives to their referents, then identify the entity filling the requested possessive or relational slot. For example, if a clue says energy from “this” is measured by an instrument, “this” refers to the source, not the energy or radiation being measured or its measurement label.
